bugs.name: Enabling minimum item quantity disables saved minimum order value
bugs.summary: Enabling Minimum quantity of items silently turns off the saved $50 Minimal order value requirement; saving and refreshing preserves the loss.
bugs.expected: The separately presented optional thresholds remain enabled together: the $50.00 Channel-USD minimum order value remains active when Minimum quantity of items is enabled.
bugs.actual: With Minimal order value enabled and saved at $50.00, enabling Minimum quantity of items immediately turned Minimal order value off and removed its amount field. After saving and refreshing, Minimal order value remained off while Minimum quantity of items remained on.
reproSteps: Start signed in as the admin account using the provided saved authentication state; no credentials were entered. Open /discounts/vouchers?asc=true&sort=code.
Create a fresh voucher named vouchers-7q4p-20260613. Add the manual code VOUCHERS-20260613-K8Q2, assign Channel-USD, select Entire order and Percentage, enter 10%, and save.

On the created voucher at /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjoxMQ%3D%3D, open Requirements, enable Minimal order value, enter 50 for Channel-USD, and save. Verify the toggle is on and the amount displays as 50.00 USD.
Enable Minimum quantity of items. Observe that Minimal order value is now off and its amount field is absent, while Minimum quantity of items is on.
Save the change, refresh the voucher page, and reopen Requirements. Confirm Minimal order value remains off and Minimum quantity of items remains on.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the reported expectation as inconsistent with intended behavior. The pre-redesign voucher UI used a radio group with NONE, ORDER and ITEM choices, and the pinned E2E tests exercise choosing one requirement type at a time. The redesign preserves that selection model with button-like controls. Therefore switching to minimum item quantity replacing minimum order value is consistent with established dashboard interaction design. Core voucher APIs can represent both fields, so this conclusion is about dashboard behavior rather than an API restriction.

bugs.name: Saleor Pulse announcement overlaps voucher Save on narrow viewports
bugs.summary: The open Saleor Pulse announcement partially overlaps the fixed voucher Save control at 414×896 and 390×844. A normal center click did not save at either size; dismissing Pulse exposed Save, and the update then completed. This establishes partial interception, not complete unreachability, and does not establish a general mobile-support policy.
bugs.expected: With the voucher Save control enabled, clicking its center should save the edited voucher rather than have the click intercepted by the promotional announcement.
bugs.actual: At 414×896 and 390×844, the open Pulse panel covered most of the fixed Save control. A center click produced no save; the edit remained pending. After dismissing Pulse, Save worked and the edited name was visible.
reproSteps: Sign in as the authorized Saleor dashboard admin using the supplied saved authentication state (no credentials or saved-state path included). In the dashboard, create a disposable voucher with a manual code, Channel-USD, Entire order / Percentage at 10%, and a QA name; save it and open its detail page.

In a fresh authenticated browser session at 414×896, navigate to /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjo2. With the default Saleor Pulse announcement open, change Voucher Name and scroll to the bottom so Save is enabled.

Click the center of Save while Pulse remains open. The edit does not save; after dismissing Pulse, Save remains available. Click Save again and verify the update completes and the edited name is visible.

Repeat in a fresh authenticated browser session at 390×844 on the same voucher detail page: change Voucher Name, scroll to the bottom, and click the center of enabled Save with Pulse open. The edit does not complete. Dismiss Pulse and click Save; the control transitions through saving and then becomes disabled. This confirms recovery, not that the first click saved.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the claim that this dismissible announcement overlap is a voucher Save bug. The supplied reproduction shows an open promotional announcement partially intercepting Save; its accessible Dismiss Pulse announcement control works, and Save succeeds after dismissal. Dismissing the announcement is the expected way to reveal the covered control. The record does not establish an undismissable overlay, a broken Save after dismissal, or a requirement that the announcement remain open while saving. This rejection is limited to the reported open-announcement overlap with mobile voucher Save and does not classify other Pulse interactions.

matchingGuidance.rejectionScope: Open, dismissible Pulse announcement partially overlaps mobile Save; dismissing it reveals a working Save control.

bugs.name: Switching through free shipping lets an existing variant be assigned again
bugs.summary: Reported claim: after saving a Products voucher as Free shipping and back, the existing variant becomes selectable again and the assigned count increases despite only one unique row.
bugs.expected: Already assigned variants remain checked and disabled in the assignment picker, and the assigned count matches the unique eligible variants.
bugs.actual: The report claimed that the existing Monospace Tee S could be selected again after the type roundtrip, producing 2 assigned with only one S row; Save then normalized the count to 1.
reproSteps: Create and save a disposable Products voucher with a unique code, an assigned sales channel, a positive percentage discount, and Monospace Tee S (SKU 328223580) assigned as an eligible variant.
Switch to Free shipping, save, and reload the saved detail.
Switch back to Products, enter a positive percentage, and save.
Open Assign variants and search the sibling SKU 328223581.
Inspect the existing Monospace Tee S (SKU 328223580): the report claims it is unchecked and selectable and can be assigned again. Compare the resulting assigned count with the unique visible rows.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection as reported after independent Mo and Codex browser checks did not reproduce it. Mo checked the Channel-PLN roundtrip; Codex independently checked Channel-USD. In both, the existing S variant remained checked and disabled, Assign stayed disabled without a new selection, and closing the picker left one assigned variant and one visible row. The pinned picker explicitly locks already assigned IDs. This rejection is scoped to the supplied roundtrip and duplicate-selection claim; it does not establish that every timing, channel or eligibility-state variant is impossible.

bugs.name: Fractional generated-code quantity is concatenated into a larger integer and creates that many codes
bugs.summary: Entering 1.5 in Code Quantity drops the decimal point, displays 15, and confirming creates 15 CODES-VALID-prefixed draft codes without an invalid-input warning.
bugs.expected: A fractional quantity should be rejected or clearly reported as invalid, rather than silently converted to another quantity.
bugs.actual: Typing 1.5 displayed 15 with Confirm enabled. Confirming generated 15 CODES-VALID-prefixed Draft code rows and showed “Unsaved changes: Codes.”
reproSteps: Sign in to the supplied Saleor fixture through its supported authentication setup and open Discounts > Vouchers.
Create and save a disposable entire-order percentage voucher with a baseline code and Channel-USD.
Open Codes > Add code > Generate codes. Starting with an empty Code Quantity, type the keys 1, decimal point, and 5 sequentially. Enter a unique code prefix.
Observe that Code Quantity visibly reads 15 before confirming. Confirm and observe fifteen local Draft code rows with Unsaved changes: Codes; use pagination to inspect the remaining rows.
For the related alias, reopen Generate codes with an empty quantity and type minus followed by 1 sequentially. Observe quantity 1 before Confirm and one additional local Draft code afterward.
Discard the generated Draft codes through Vouchers > Ignore changes. The generated codes remain local and unsaved during the reported flow.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this report as intended integer input validation, not an issue. The controlled Code Quantity field discards unsupported decimal-point and intermediate-minus keystrokes. Sequentially typing 1.5 visibly leaves 15 before Confirm; typing minus followed by 1 visibly leaves 1. Confirm generates exactly the displayed accepted integer count as local, unsaved Draft codes. This intended behavior should not be flagged as a bug.

matchingGuidance.rejectionScope: The reported sequential typing of 1.5 or minus followed by 1: unsupported decimal-point and intermediate-minus edits are discarded, the accepted integer 15 or 1 is visible before Confirm, and confirmation generates that displayed count as local, unsaved Draft codes.

bugs.name: Fixed-amount required error persists after entering a valid amount
bugs.summary: A zero fixed-amount Save returns a required-field error; entering 5.00 and blurring retains that last submission error.
bugs.expected: After changing the amount to a valid positive value and blurring the field, the required-field error and red outline should clear.
bugs.actual: Channel-USD displays 5.00 USD but still shows “This field is required” and a red outline after blur and after navigating from Discount to Details and back.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher.
Enter a unique voucher name, add a unique manual code, assign Channel-USD, and choose Entire order with Fixed amount.
Set the Channel-USD amount to 0 and click Save. Observe “This field is required” and the red outline.
Replace 0 with 5 and blur the field. Navigate to Details and back to Discount; observe 5.00 USD while the required-field message and red outline remain.
bugs.reason: This follows the dashboard’s server-submission feedback convention: Customer email and Attribute label errors also remain after correcting and blurring, then clear on the next successful Save. Voucher amount edits update draft values without revalidating the previous server response. The retained message is not a bug; this finding’s clear-on-edit expectation does not apply to these submission errors.

bugs.name: Negative Channel-PLN percentage silently becomes positive
bugs.summary: Typing -5 into the saved Channel-PLN percentage field visibly changed it to 5; Save succeeded, a “Voucher updated” confirmation appeared, and the saved field remained 5%.
bugs.expected: The negative percentage should be rejected with visible validation and should not be silently converted into a different, positive discount.
bugs.actual: From a saved Channel-PLN value of 0, normal keyboard entry of -5 displayed 5 without validation. Save succeeded with a “Voucher updated” confirmation, and 5% remained saved.
reproSteps: Using the authenticated fixture session (the dashboard showed admin@example.com), navigate through Discounts > Vouchers at /discounts/vouchers.

Create a fresh voucher named NEGPLN-PCT-20261013-7341 with unique code MOM-PLN-5F8A2D91C63E, assign Channel-PLN, choose Percentage, and save. To create the voucher, use 1% initially; then edit its Discount section, set Channel-PLN to 0, save, reload, and reopen Discount to confirm the saved 0.
On the voucher at /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlOjE0NA%3D, focus the Channel-PLN percentage field, press Control+A, and type -5 using normal keyboard input.
Observe that the field displays 5 with no validation, then click Save and verify the “Voucher updated” confirmation and persisted 5% value.
bugs.reason: Human review confirmed this is intentional nonnegative discount input formatting, not a bug. A discount percentage cannot be negative: the input filters the minus sign and displays the accepted nonnegative value before Save. Saving that displayed percentage is correct behavior. The reported expectation that a filtered minus keystroke must produce a validation error or prevent saving the displayed valid discount is rejected.

bugs.name: Minimum quantity requirement changes from 4 to 3 after refresh
bugs.summary: The report attributes a minimum item quantity changing from 4 to 3 to Save and refresh. Human review identified scrolling inside the quantity input as the interaction that changed the draft value.
bugs.expected: After saving and refreshing, Minimum quantity of items remains enabled and displays the submitted quantity of 4.
bugs.actual: The report describes 4 before Save and 3 after refresh, with Minimum quantity of items still enabled.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers.
Create a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, set a valid 10% discount, leave Minimum Requirements disabled, and save.
Open the saved voucher, enable Minimum quantity of items, enter 4, and click Save.
Refresh the voucher and inspect the enabled quantity field; the report claims it displays 3.
bugs.reason: Human review confirmed this is not a bug: scrolling inside the quantity input changed the displayed draft from 4 to 3 before Save. Save and refresh preserved the submitted value rather than decrementing it. Independent UI verification submitted 4, received 4 from the API, and retained 4 after reload. The pinned quantity field is a number input with step 1, and the save handler preserves an integer 4. The separately accepted fractional-input truncation defect does not apply to this report.

bugs.name: Channel percentage is reduced by one point on save
bugs.summary: A fresh Entire order Percentage voucher with only Channel-PLN assigned changes its entered 10% value to 9% after saving; the 9% value remains after a full page refresh.
bugs.expected: After saving and refreshing, the Channel-PLN percentage field should still show the entered value of 10%.
bugs.actual: The field showed 10 before saving, then showed 9 after save and continued to show 9 after refreshing the voucher details page.
reproSteps: At a 375×812 viewport, open /discounts/vouchers and use the supplied authenticated Admin session.
Create a new test-owned voucher named MOMENTIC-CHANNEL-PCT-10-Q7Z9 and add the unique manual code MOCHAN10Q7Z9.
Select Entire order and Percentage, and assign only Channel-PLN.
Enter 10 in the Channel-PLN percentage field and verify it displays 10 before saving.
Save the voucher. On its details page, observe that the Channel-PLN percentage field displays 9.
Refresh the details page and inspect the Channel-PLN percentage field again; it still displays 9.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this finding: scrolling over the focused percentage number input changes the visible draft from 10 to 9 before Save. Scrolling outside the input does not cause the change. Save persists the already displayed 9; it does not reduce a submitted 10. The recording independently shows the user-triggered input change about 6.3 seconds before the Save click. This rejection covers the reported wheel interaction and alleged save-time decrement, not a value changing during Save without prior input interaction or the separately accepted fractional-input and percentage-validation defects.

matchingGuidance.rejectionScope: The scroll passes over the focused percentage input and changes its draft value before Save; scrolling outside does not fail.

bugs.name: Blank voucher start time defaults to midnight
bugs.summary: Leaving the optional Start Hour completely blank (--:--), with no hour or minute entered, saves the selected start date at 00:00 (12:00 AM). This is the dashboard’s intended default for an unset time.
bugs.expected: Leaving Start Hour completely blank should use midnight (00:00, displayed as 12:00 AM) on the selected start date.
bugs.actual: Saving with a selected start date and a completely blank Start Hour uses midnight on that date.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher.
Enter a unique voucher name and manual code, assign a channel, and set a valid entire-order percentage discount.
Choose a future start date and leave Start Hour completely blank (--:--), without entering an hour or minute.
Click Save and inspect the Schedule card; the selected date uses 12:00 AM (00:00).
bugs.reason: Human review confirmed that a completely blank optional Start Hour correctly defaults to midnight (12:00 AM). The dashboard’s joinDateTime helper explicitly uses 00:00 when time is unset. This rejection applies only when no hour or minute was entered. A partially entered time such as 10:00 -- is a different case: changing its entered hour and minute to midnight is not covered by this rejection.

bugs.name: Negative minimum order value silently becomes positive and persists
bugs.summary: Sequentially typing -1 into the voucher’s Minimal order value field filters the minus sign and visibly displays 1.00 USD before Save. Saving and reopening retains that displayed positive amount.
bugs.expected: A negative minimum order value should be rejected with visible validation, preventing Save until the value is valid.
bugs.actual: Typing -1 and blurring displayed 1.00 USD without a validation message. Save succeeded, and the reopened voucher retained Minimal order value enabled at 1.00 USD.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher.
Enter a unique voucher name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, choose Entire order and Percentage, and set a valid 10% discount.
Enable Minimal order value, type the minus and 1 keys sequentially in the Channel-USD amount field, and press Tab. Observe the displayed 1.00 USD before Save.
Click Save, reopen the voucher from the Vouchers list, and confirm Minimal order value remains enabled at 1.00 USD.
bugs.reason: Human review confirmed this is intended unsigned monetary input filtering, not a bug. VoucherRequirements uses PriceFieldV2, whose formatter removes the minus sign and displays the accepted positive amount before submission. Save preserves that visible 1.00 USD value; it does not silently change a submitted negative amount. This rejection covers the reported sequential typing of -1, not an unverified claim that a negative amount reaches storage.

bugs.name: Blank voucher start date defaults to the current date
bugs.summary: Leaving the entire optional Start Date blank is accepted and defaults the saved voucher start to the current date and time. This is intentional defaulting, not a requirement that Save reject an unset date.
bugs.expected: A genuinely blank Start Date may use the current date and time when the voucher is saved.
bugs.actual: Creating a voucher with Start Date completely blank succeeds; the saved Schedule displays the current date, which remains present after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher.
Enter a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, and configure a valid Entire order discount of 10%.
Leave Start Date completely blank, with no date segments entered, and click Save.
Inspect the saved Schedule and reload the voucher; the default current start date is displayed and retained.
bugs.reason: Human review accepts defaulting a genuinely unset date. The dashboard sends null for an empty date, and the backend start-date field explicitly defaults to the current time. This rejection covers the default itself, not visibly partial date input or the separately accepted edit-form failure to display the saved default.

bugs.name: Same-day end-time validation displays an inaccurate date error
bugs.summary: Rejected wording-only complaint: the end-before-start error allegedly becomes inaccurate when the calendar dates match. Date includes hours, so the message and timestamp rejection are already correct.
bugs.expected: The rejected report asks for different wording solely because the calendar dates match. No wording change is required: date includes hours, so June 1 at 09:30 is before June 1 at 10:00. This reference does not reject a report identifying missing End Hour error styling.
bugs.actual: Before Save, both calendar dates are June 1, 2030, with Start Hour 10:00 AM and End Hour 09:30 AM. After Save, the earlier combined timestamp is correctly rejected with “End date cannot be before the start date.” A wording-only report calls this message inaccurate because the calendar dates match; that expectation is rejected. A 10:30 AM end saves successfully.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers. Create and save a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, Channel-PLN, and a valid 10% entire-order discount.
In Schedule, set Start Date and End Date to June 1, 2030, Start Hour to 10:00 AM and End Hour to 09:30 AM. Click Save.
Observe the rejected Save and “End date cannot be before the start date” message beneath End Date.
Keep the same dates, change End Hour to 10:30 AM and click Save. Observe successful saving and “Voucher updated.”
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the claim that the date wording is inaccurate. Date includes hours: June 1, 2030 at 09:30 is before June 1, 2030 at 10:00. The backend compares complete DateTime values and correctly rejects this earlier end with “End date cannot be before the start date.” The same-day 10:30 end saves successfully. Both the chronological validation and this wording are acceptable; time-specific wording is not required. This rejection concerns the initial error wording, not stale errors after correction, failed validation, or stale values and dirty state after a successful Save. Missing error styling on End Hour is a separate human-approved severity-1 presentation bug; a finding identifying that omission must not be rejected by this wording-only reference.

matchingScope.rejectedFailureClaim: Only the alleged inaccuracy of the end-before-start wording when calendar dates match; no missing End Hour indication is established by this claim.
matchingScope.beforeAndAfterReview: The same accurate message and timestamp validation may remain. No product change is needed for this wording-only complaint.
matchingScope.excludedAcceptedFailure: Date-only error styling that leaves End Hour unmarked is a separate accepted severity-1 failure. Its observation is not invalidated by this wording rejection.
matchingScope.negativeExample: The app says end date before start date even though both dates are June 1, so the message is wrong.
matchingScope.acceptedCounterexample: The earlier end time is correctly rejected, but only End Date is red and End Hour has no error indication; both should be marked.

matchingGuidance.acceptedCounterpart: Same-day end-before-start validation highlights End Date but leaves End Hour unmarked

bugs.name: Voucher schedule validation error persists after correcting the end date/time
bugs.summary: An end-before-start Save error remains after restoring the saved valid schedule and blurring. The form shows the last submission’s validation response, while Save is disabled because the restored dates and times match the saved values.
bugs.expected: After restoring a valid end date and time later than the start, the validation message and invalid field styling should clear without another submission.
bugs.actual: Save rejected an end of 01/01/2020 at 08:30 AM before a start of 01/01/2020 at 09:30 AM. Restoring the saved end of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM left the red End Date outline and “End date cannot be before the start date” message visible after blur. Save was disabled because the restored schedule was unchanged.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers > Create voucher.
Enter a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-PLN, and set a valid 10% entire-order discount.
Set Start Date to 01/01/2020 at 09:30 AM and enable an end date of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM. Save the voucher.
Change the saved end to 01/01/2020 at 08:30 AM and click Save. Observe the end-before-start validation message.
Restore the saved end of 01/02/2020 at 09:30 AM and blur. Observe the retained message and disabled Save button.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this as the dashboard’s normal submit-time validation convention. Editing and blurring draft fields do not clear the last server submission error; validation is refreshed by a later submission, and a successful submission clears that feedback. Customer and Attribute forms use the same convention. Restoring the saved schedule makes the form unchanged, so disabling Save is correct and does not indicate a failed save. Retaining this previous error after correction is not a bug. This rejection does not cover stale schedule values or a false Unsaved warning after a successful Save.

bugs.name: Scheduled voucher status filter does not filter the voucher list
bugs.summary: The report claims applying Status is Scheduled leaves Active vouchers visible, omits a future voucher, and loses the filter condition. Independent fixture verification instead retained the Scheduled filter and showed only the future voucher.
bugs.expected: Applying Status is Scheduled should show scheduled vouchers, including the newly created future voucher, and exclude Active vouchers.
bugs.actual: The report claims the filter panel closed while the list remained unfiltered with Active rows and no scheduled voucher; reopening Filters showed a blank condition, and repeating selection and Apply produced the same result.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and open Discounts > Vouchers.
Create a disposable voucher with a unique name and manual code, assign Channel-USD, set a valid 10% discount, and set Start Date to 01/01/2030. Save and confirm its details show Scheduled.
Return to All vouchers, open Filters, and select Status / is / Scheduled.
Click Apply and inspect the list. Reopen Filters and repeat the selection and Apply; the report claims Active rows remain, the scheduled voucher is omitted, and the condition disappears.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this reported failure as a hallucination. Independent verification on the pinned fixture showed the Scheduled condition persisted in the URL, query request, and reopened filter panel. The resulting list included the independently created future voucher and excluded Active and Ended vouchers. Applying the filter and retaining its condition worked correctly; the report’s alleged unfiltered list and lost condition were contradicted by the verified UI behavior.

bugs.name: Pasting negative minimum-order amounts saves a positive first amount and ignores the second row
bugs.summary: The report claims pasting a two-line column of -10.50 and -20.75 into the PLN Minimal order value field silently saves PLN 10.50 and leaves USD unchanged.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the pasted column to fill down to USD, or the negative values to be rejected with a validation error.
bugs.actual: PLN displays 10.50 before Save, USD keeps 200.75, no validation appears, and both values persist after Save and reload.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture administrator and create a voucher with Channel-PLN and Channel-USD, a fixed amount of 5 for each, and Minimal order value PLN 100.25 / USD 200.75.
Paste the two-line text -10.50 and -20.75 into the PLN Minimal order value field after selecting its contents, then blur.
Observe PLN 10.50 and USD 200.75 without an error, then Save and reload.
bugs.reason: The observed behavior is intended. The spreadsheet column paste skips invalid cells by design, and sanitizeSpreadsheetPrice treats negative values as invalid, so neither row fills down. The browser's ordinary paste then goes through the unsigned monetary formatter, which removes the minus sign, as the existing Negative minimum order value rejection already established. The positive amount is visible before Save, and Save preserves exactly that displayed value. The fill-down hint covers valid amounts and promises nothing about negative cells. The post-run reproducer confirmed the observations, not that they are a defect.

bugs.name: Voucher header omits the percentage discount value
bugs.summary: The report claims a saved single-channel 10% voucher's header pill should read Entire order · 10% instead of Entire order · %.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the header pill to include the configured percentage.
bugs.actual: The header pill shows Entire order · % while the Channel-PLN field shows 10.
reproSteps: Create a voucher with a unique manual code, only Channel-PLN, Entire order and Percentage 10. Save and reload.
Compare the Entire order · % header pill with the 10% channel value.
bugs.reason: Intended. The header pill labels the voucher's scope and discount type, not its amount: getVoucherTypePillLabel renders scope plus % or Fixed, and its unit test expects exactly Entire order · %. Percentages can differ by channel and are shown in the Discount section. The post-run reproducer reached the same conclusion.

bugs.name: Saving zero minimum order value turns the requirement off
bugs.summary: Saving zero minimum order value turns the requirement off.
bugs.expected: Saving should be blocked while an 'Invalid minimum spend' error is present, or the zero amount should be handled with clear feedback.
bugs.actual: Save completes successfully with a checkmark, but reloading the voucher shows the Minimal order value toggle switched off.
reproSteps: Create a fresh unique REQ-QA voucher with Channel-PLN and a 10% entire-order discount.
Enable Minimal order value and save a positive amount such as 12.34 PLN.
Change the enabled amount to 0, blur, and click Save.
After Voucher updated, refresh and scroll to Minimum Requirements.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: a minimum order value of 0 means no minimum, so the requirement shows as off after saving.

bugs.name: Fixed amount bulk paste silently skips negative values and truncates precision
bugs.summary: Fixed amount bulk paste silently skips negative values and truncates precision.
bugs.expected: Invalid or truncated pasted values should be validated with clear user feedback rather than silently skipping a row or truncating precision without notice.
bugs.actual: Channel-PLN remains unchanged at 31.25 while Channel-USD updates to 22.34 without any validation warning, and saving reports 'Voucher updated' with the values persisting on reload.
reproSteps: Create a unique DISC-QA voucher with code and PLN/USD channels. Select Products and Fixed amount.
Save fixed amounts PLN 31.25 and USD 42.50.
Copy a two-line column containing -5 then 22.345, focus the PLN amount and paste.
Observe PLN remains 31.25 while USD becomes 22.34; click Save.
Observe Voucher updated and reopen the voucher; amounts remain 31.25 and 22.34.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: bulk paste skips invalid cells such as negatives and limits amounts to the currency's decimal places, the same as typing.

bugs.name: Products voucher saves without required eligible assignments
bugs.summary: Products voucher saves without required eligible assignments.
bugs.expected: Saving is blocked with validation feedback until at least one category, collection, product, or variant is assigned.
bugs.actual: The voucher saves successfully with a 'Voucher updated' notification and updates the header badge to 'Products · %' with all assignment groups remaining empty.
reproSteps: As the administrator, create a fresh ELIG-QA-* voucher with a manual code, both available channels and 10% discount for each channel; save.
Select Products under What the voucher discounts.
Leave categories, collections and products/variants unassigned and click Save.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the edit page deliberately lets a voucher be saved before setup is finished and tracks the missing catalogue as a pending "Required to redeem" step ("Finish them now or come back later"). An empty catalogue doesn't apply to any line items, so nothing is corrupted.

bugs.name: Stale voucher discount save erases a newer saved name
bugs.summary: Stale voucher discount save erases a newer saved name.
bugs.expected: Saving a distinct discount field should preserve the newer saved voucher name, or show a conflict requiring resolution rather than silently losing the rename.
bugs.actual: Save showed Voucher updated; after refresh the name had reverted to QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-JORDAN and percentage was 23.
reproSteps: As Maya staff, create a unique QA-MULTI voucher with one code, entire-order percentage discount and Channel-PLN assigned; save it.
Open its detail in tab A with name QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-JORDAN and percentage 17.
Open the same voucher in tab B, rename to QA-MULTI-MAYA-0723-TAB2, save and refresh to confirm persistence.
Switch back to tab A without refreshing. Confirm it still shows the original name and 17%.
Change only Channel-PLN percentage to 23 and Save.
Refresh tab A and inspect saved name and percentage.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: saving from a stale tab overwrites a newer concurrent edit, which is last-write-wins. Like Metabase's concurrent-edit labels, the app isn't expected to merge or detect conflicting saves.

bugs.name: Clearing the only draft name still triggers an unsaved-changes warning
bugs.summary: Clearing the only draft name still triggers an unsaved-changes warning.
bugs.expected: After restoring the edited Voucher Name field to its initial blank state, clicking Back navigates back without an unsaved changes warning.
bugs.actual: A 'Leave without saving changes?' confirmation dialog appears upon clicking Back.
reproSteps: As administrator, open a fresh Create Voucher form with no prerequisites or settings edited.
Enter EDIT-newdraft-undo in Voucher Name.
Select all text in Voucher Name, press Backspace and blur the field.
Click Back in the bottom action bar.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the unsaved-changes warning tracks whether the form was edited, not whether it returns to its original values, so typing and clearing a name still warns.

bugs.name: Usage limit / minimum quantity fields can't be cleared: they jump back to 1, so retyping gives the wrong number
bugs.summary: Usage limit / minimum quantity fields can't be cleared: they jump back to 1, so retyping gives the wrong number.
bugs.expected: Clearing the field leaves it empty (or checks it only on blur/save), so select-all + type '5' gives 5.
bugs.actual: After Ctrl+A + Backspace the value is instantly '1'; typing '5' then gives '15'. Saving sent usageLimit '15' and minCheckoutItemsQuantity 13, and both persisted after reload.
reproSteps: Open /discounts/vouchers and open 'Big order discount'
Turn on 'Limit number of times this discount can be used in total' (value defaults to 1)
Click the Limit of Uses input, press Ctrl+A then Backspace: the field shows 1 instead of being empty
Type 5: the field shows 15
Do the same with 'Minimum quantity of items' and type 3: it shows 13
Save and reload: usage limit 15 and min quantity 13 are saved
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: clearing the field and typing a new value saves the new value.

bugs.name: Manual code dialog shows 'Code already exists' for a new, unique code and stays open
bugs.summary: Manual code dialog shows 'Code already exists' for a new, unique code and stays open.
bugs.expected: A unique code is added once and the dialog closes without an error.
bugs.actual: The dialog stays open, the input is marked red with 'Code already exists', and the code (e.g. UNIQ456) already appears in the Voucher codes table. The checklist reads '2 codes ready'.
reproSteps: Open /discounts/vouchers/add
Enter Voucher Name 'X'
Click Add code > Manual code
Type the unique code 'UNIQ456' and click Confirm
The dialog stays open showing 'Code already exists'
Click Back: the table lists UNIQ456 once and the checklist says '2 codes ready'
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: confirming a unique code adds it once and closes the dialog.

bugs.name: New voucher availability says two channels despite none assigned
bugs.summary: New voucher availability says two channels despite none assigned.
bugs.expected: Availability summary reports no assigned channels.
bugs.actual: Availability says Voucher in 2 of 2 channels while the card immediately below says No channels assigned and setup remains 0 of 3.
reproSteps: Open Vouchers.
Click Create voucher without assigning any channels.
Read Availability.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: an untouched Create Voucher form shows 0 of 2 channels with No channels assigned.

bugs.name: Adding a condition clears an unapplied voucher filter
bugs.summary: Adding a condition clears an unapplied voucher filter.
bugs.expected: The configured condition row is retained and a second condition row is added.
bugs.actual: The configured condition fields are reset to empty placeholders and no additional condition row is added.
reproSteps: Open the voucher list as an authenticated administrator and clear any applied filters.
Open Filters and configure Status is Expired without clicking Apply.
Click Add condition.
Inspect the filter panel.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: a completed filter condition survives Add condition; only unfinished rows are removed.

bugs.name: Negative voucher generation quantity silently closes the dialog
bugs.summary: Pasting -1 into Code Quantity enables Confirm. Confirming closes the dialog without generating codes or showing validation feedback.
bugs.expected: A negative code count is rejected with disabled Confirm or a clear validation message, retaining the dialog for correction.
bugs.actual: Confirm is enabled for -1, closes the dialog, leaves original codes unchanged, and shows no error or validation anywhere. Whole-page assertion confirmed the missing feedback.
reproSteps: Create and save a disposable QA-GENCODES voucher with generated codes, Channel-USD and 10% discount.
Choose Add code > Generate codes.
Paste -1 into Code Quantity (max 50).
Click enabled Confirm.
Observe unchanged voucher codes table and feedback.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Saving zero item minimum silently removes the requirement
bugs.summary: Saving zero item minimum silently removes the requirement.
bugs.expected: The displayed minimum-one-item validation prevents saving 0, retaining the invalid input for correction and the previous saved configuration.
bugs.actual: Save removes the quantity input and disables both minimum modes; this persists after reload. A whole-page assertion confirmed no validation error remained and Save was disabled.
reproSteps: Assign Channel-PLN and Channel-USD; set both percentage discounts to 10%. Enable minimal order value with 100.25 PLN and 25.50 USD and save.
Open Requirements; set PLN minimum to 0 and save, then reload.
Switch to Minimum quantity of items, enter 0 and blur. Observe “Enter at least 1 item.”
Click Save, allow the update to settle, and reload the voucher's Requirements.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: the field says to enter at least 1 item; a minimum of 0 means no minimum requirement, as with vouchers-b08.

bugs.name: Failed quantity save hides requirement inputs and turns toggles off
bugs.summary: Failed quantity save hides requirement inputs and turns toggles off.
bugs.expected: Saving should be rejected with a visible field validation error while retaining the enabled control and entered value so the user can correct it.
bugs.actual: A “Couldn't save voucher” toast directs the user to check highlighted fields, but both minimum requirement toggles turn off and the quantity input field disappears, leaving no highlighted field visible to correct.
reproSteps: Create fresh DISC-prefixed voucher with unique manual code, Channel-USD and Free shipping, then Save.
Enable Minimal order value, enter 2 USD and Save successfully.
Enable Minimum quantity of items and enter -1.
Save and inspect the requirements section.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce through the UI: the minimum-quantity field blocks typing or pasting a minus sign, so a negative quantity can only be set programmatically.

bugs.name: Saving a daylight-saving schedule silently changes the start hour
bugs.summary: Saving a daylight-saving schedule silently changes the start hour.
bugs.expected: If the entered local time cannot occur due to daylight saving, explain and reject it or request correction rather than silently saving a different hour.
bugs.actual: Start Hour changes from 02:30 AM to 03:30 AM after Save and remains 03:30 AM after reload. Default multimodal assertion confirmed no warning or validation message anywhere explaining the change.
reproSteps: Browser timezone America/Los_Angeles, desktop 1920x1080. Original observation used an already saved own fixture; verification should create a fresh fixture as described.
Open Vouchers as the supplied admin and click Create voucher.
Create a fresh uniquely named TIME-prefixed voucher. Add a unique manual code, assign Channel-USD using Availability Manage, and enter a 10% entire-order discount.
Set Start Date to March 14, 2027 and Start Hour to 02:30 AM. Enable Set end date and set End Date March 14, 2027, End Hour 04:00 AM. Verify entered fields before saving.
Click Save and inspect Start Hour and feedback.
Reload the saved voucher and inspect Start Hour again.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: 02:30 AM on March 14, 2027 does not exist in America/Los_Angeles (clocks jump from 2:00 to 3:00), so it resolves to 03:30 AM, the same instant.

bugs.name: Negative fixed discount silently becomes positive
bugs.summary: Negative fixed discount silently becomes positive.
bugs.expected: Reject a negative discount with understandable validation rather than silently converting it to a positive discount.
bugs.actual: The saved and refreshed voucher shows 1.00 PLN. USD also shows 12.34 after entering 12.345. A whole-page multimodal assertion confirmed no error or rounding warning appeared.
reproSteps: As vouchers admin, create a fresh QA-DISCOUNT voucher with a unique manual code and PLN/USD availability; save valid percentage values.
Open Discount and switch to Fixed amount.
Enter -1 for Channel-PLN and 12.345 for Channel-USD.
Save, refresh, and reopen Discount.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review.

bugs.name: Saved percentage differs from the displayed input
bugs.summary: Saved percentage differs from the displayed input.
bugs.expected: The saved percentage should equal the displayed 12%.
bugs.actual: The refreshed Channel-USD input shows 11%, not the displayed 12% that was saved.
reproSteps: At 1440 × 900, open Vouchers as the authenticated admin and create a fresh private QA-RESP voucher with one manual code, Channel-USD availability, Entire order percentage 10, and a matching name. Save.
Resize to 768 × 900 and scroll to Percentage for Channel-USD.
Replace 10 with 12. In the observed run the keyboard entry displayed 112; replace that entire value with 12 and verify it displays 12.
Scroll to the bottom and click Save. Observe the Voucher updated confirmation.
Refresh, wait for the voucher to load, and scroll to the Channel-USD percentage.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Cleared monetary requirement stays marked unsaved after successful save and reload
bugs.summary: Cleared monetary requirement stays marked unsaved after successful save and reload.
bugs.expected: After successfully saving the voucher with a cleared minimum order value, the unsaved changes state should clear and the Save button should disable (or, if a blank value is disallowed, display a validation error rather than a success notification).
bugs.actual: A “Voucher updated” notification appears, yet “Unsaved changes: Channels” remains in the footer and the Save button stays enabled.
reproSteps: Create a fresh QA-REQ Free shipping voucher with unique code and Channel-USD assigned.
Enable Minimal order value and enter 20.25 USD. Save.
Clear the USD value, blur, click Save and wait at least 3 seconds.
Observe Voucher updated and Unsaved changes: Channels together.
Reload and open Requirements without editing.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Changing voucher scope loses the percentage edit on save
bugs.summary: Changing voucher scope loses the percentage edit on save.
bugs.expected: Channel-PLN percentage input should accept the entered value (5%) and persist it after save and reload.
bugs.actual: Channel-PLN percentage immediately reverts to 75% upon typing and remains 75% after saving and reloading.
reproSteps: As admin open Percentage order discount.
Set PLN percentage to 7.5, save, then change scope to Products and save.
Change scope to Entire order, enter 5 in Channel-PLN percentage, then Save.
Reload and inspect Discount.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review.

bugs.name: Whitespace voucher name leaves an unidentified list row
bugs.summary: Whitespace voucher name leaves an unidentified list row.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only name should be treated as unnamed and show an identifying fallback (such as its code), or be rejected with validation rather than producing an unidentified list row.
bugs.actual: Save succeeds. After refresh and Back, the voucher row's Name cell shows only “1 code”; neither the voucher name nor its code is displayed.
reproSteps: As authenticated admin, create a fresh voucher with unique NAME-prefixed code and NAME-prefixed name, one available channel and entire-order 10% discount; save.
Change Voucher Name to exactly three ordinary spaces and Save.
Verify Voucher updated appears, then refresh and use Back to return to All vouchers.
Inspect the voucher's Name cell.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: voucher name is optional (internal staff name), so a whitespace-only name is treated as unnamed and the row falls back to the code count.

bugs.name: Adding a channel with blank minimum order value makes Save silently fail
bugs.summary: After adding a channel to voucher availability, clicking Save displays a 'Voucher updated' confirmation toast but leaves 'Unsaved changes: Channels' displayed in the footer.
bugs.expected: Saving the voucher should clear the 'Unsaved changes: Channels' status indicator.
bugs.actual: A 'Voucher updated' confirmation toast appears, but 'Unsaved changes: Channels' remains visible in the footer.
reproSteps: Do not edit linked channels. Observed on QA-CHANNEL-availability, voucher Vm91Y2hlcjo4 at desktop width 1440. Earlier the voucher had both channels; USD was removed and saved immediately before being re-added. Use a fresh equivalent voucher; if direct initial addition differs, also remove a previously configured USD channel, save, and re-add it.
As primary admin, create a separate QA-CHANNEL-prefixed voucher with a manual code, Free shipping type and Channel-PLN assigned.
Enable Minimal order value, enter 80 PLN and save.
In Availability Manage, select Channel-USD and confirm two channels.
Leave the newly displayed USD minimum order value blank and click Save.
bugs.reason: Cannot reproduce on human review: clearing the minimum order value shows a field validation error.

bugs.name: Mobile codes table hides the code identifiers without a way to expand them
bugs.summary: At 390px width the voucher code text receives only 50px, making every generated code with the same prefix look identical (QAM...). Tapping a code reveals copy/delete icons but never its identifier; the table has no horizontal scrolling or full-text tooltip.
bugs.expected: Staff should be able to read or reveal enough of each code to distinguish it before selecting, copying, or deleting it, including at mobile width.
bugs.actual: Twelve different QAMOBILE-prefixed generated codes all display QAM... at 390×844. Tapping a code leaves it truncated. The code span has clientWidth 50 and scrollWidth 370, no title or expand action, and the table has clientWidth and scrollWidth of 316, so horizontal scroll cannot reveal it.
reproSteps: Sign in and open /discounts/vouchers/add at a 390px-wide viewport.
In Voucher codes, choose Add code → Generate codes, quantity 3 and prefix QAMOBILE, then Confirm. No saving is needed to see the failure.
Scroll to the codes table and try to identify any one generated code.
Tap its code text and try horizontal scrolling. Observe all rows remain QAM... with no full identifier displayed.
bugs.reason: Works as intended per human review: truncated codes on mobile can still be copied.
